title: Cascode CS amp
description: A telescopic (non-boosted) cascode common-source stage: a common-source input device with a cascode device stacked in series on top, driving a current-source load. The cascode raises the stage output resistance to about $A_{v0,casc}/g_{ds,in}$, so the gain is no longer limited by the input device's own output resistance but by whatever the load presents - here a plain current source, so the load's $g_{ds}$ sets the ceiling. All three devices are composed children carrying the same branch current: the input and cascode in series (the parent cascode bind carries the input's drain current), and the current-source load in parallel at the output. Set load_sign to -1 for a signed-PMOS load table.

params.name: V_out
params.note: output DC level; sets the cascode and load drain-source voltages

params.name: V_x
params.note: cascode source (input drain) DC level: raise it for input-device headroom, lower it for cascode headroom

params.name: Av_target
params.note: a cascode buys a large gain

params.name: I_bias
params.note: branch current, shared by all three devices

params.name: gm_id_in
params.note: input-pair inversion: sets the stage gm, noise, and gain

params.name: gm_id_casc
params.note: cascode-device inversion: higher av0_casc boosts the output resistance

params.name: gm_id_load
params.note: load inversion: a longer/lower-gm/ID load raises the load output resistance (and the gain)

params.name: L
params.note: shared by the input and cascode devices

params.name: load_sign
params.note: vds sign convention of the load table: +1 for an N-style axis, -1 for a signed-PMOS axis

doc.title: Common-source input device
doc.description: The input device at the branch current. Its drain sits at V_x, one cascode source below the cascode device; it exposes its transconductance, output conductance, drain current (carried up by the cascode), and channel-noise density.

doc.title: Current-source load device
doc.description: One device biased as a current source at the branch current, exposing the output conductance that sets the cascode stage's gain ceiling, its transconductance (drain-noise scale), and its saturation headroom.

params.name: vds_l
params.note: signed to this table's axis convention

rows.name: Rout_casc
rows.note: cascode output resistance: the input device's ro boosted by (1 + cascode av0), in series with the cascode ro

rows.name: Rout
rows.note: the cascode output in parallel with the current-source load's output resistance - the load's gds now sets the ceiling. The gain assumes a capacitive load, so nothing here models a resistive one; this row is what a composing parent checks its own loading against

rows.name: Av
rows.note: input transconductance into the full cascoded output resistance

rows.name: vn_in
rows.note: input device plus the load's own density referred by gm_load/gm_in; the cascode device's own channel noise is degenerated by the input ro and neglected

rows.name: cgg_in
rows.note: estimate: the capacitance the input terminal presents — the input device's gate capacitance. Gate capacitance only, because the Miller term needs the gate-drain fraction and these tables do not carry it, so a driving stage sees more than this. No rule reads it

rows.name: I_q
rows.note: estimate: quiescent supply current — the one branch these rows model; the cascode and the load sit in it and carry the same current. The datasheet line for comparing designs; no rule reads it

rules.note: cascode gm/ID cannot exceed the weak-inversion ceiling of the data
input device saturated: its drain V_x sits above its saturation voltage
cascode device saturated: the output minus the intermediate node clears its saturation voltage
load device saturated: its headroom is the supply minus the output level
computed from the gamma-model floor; this table carries no measured noise; the simulator owns noise sign-off
input gm over the load capacitance
